The exact logarithmic expansion for each summand, its bounded tails, and compact uniform vanishing yield log J_s(n)=sn log(n/log n)+n(s log s-s)+o(n), with a strict unique saddle. Finitely many block-idempotent maps and strict convexity of x log x prove every claimed n-speed rate and rank convergence. The five enumerations and 2000-point log-rate tests are corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2014 Dolinka–East theorem already enumerates every finite idempotent and yields the conditional weights used here; no exact finite enumeration is claimed as novel. The present theorem supplies explicit large-n exponential probability rates for EVERY prescribed block-idempotent map, optimizes all exact image-block strata, and proves image-rank concentration through a uniform saddle calculation. The 2014 and 2015 papers and the inspected partial-idempotent work do not state these limits. The earlier wreath-product asymptotics assume a fixed finite group base and a growing top-level set, rather than a growing transformation base with fixed top-level size. Priority remains qualified because known exact formulas imply that the rates are computable and an unlocated general saddle theorem might directly imply them.
residual_risks: A published or unpublished asymptotic saddle evaluation derived from the 2014 exact formula may be equivalent to the rate law.
A general wreath-product probability theorem outside the inspected results could cover the fixed-m block-size-asymptotic regime.
